notes.text: Starting the alarm investigation — pulling the alarm details first.
Alarm is an out-of-spec reading just over the limit — checking that lot's history next.
Seen the alarm lot's path — now surveying all chambers to see if this one stands out.
One chamber looks consistently high with heavy wafer count — checking its thickness trend for buildup drift.
Trend shows sustained high thickness — ruling out clean and metrology effects with a commonality check.
Signal isolates to the deposition step — now checking sensors to exclude a false reading.
Sensors look normal — verifying maintenance history to confirm buildup as the driver.
Evidence points to chamber buildup drift — filing the disposition to hold the lot and chamber.

public: US Patent 6,512,991, Reducing deposition variation by modeling post-clean chamber performance
Material builds up on the chamber's inner surfaces with use and changes the deposition rate.
sources.practitioner: Deposition shows buildup more clearly than etch: material collects inside the chamber and the rate usually rises with it. Fabs compensate by wafer count since PM, which hides most but not all of the drift.
